item.title: 26 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar

A late night dinner after a day wandering the city. Today a small hole-in-the-wall shop near Da’an forest park. Some kind of fried pork, teriyaki sauce, iceberg salad, sweet potato, and black rice, with a quick melon flavoured bubble tea afterwards.

item.title: 25 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar →Next day

Today I decided to walk in a new direction from my apartment that I usually don’t go in — away from the mrt — because I had seen some places to eat at when I came home yesterday. Turns out there is a whole street teaming with activity just nearby. With a Typhoon currently travelling over the Ryukyu islands, a bowl of hot beef noodles braised in soy sauce is always a good choice.

item.title: 24 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar →Next day

I went to the store today and, due to the constant heat, was craving some watermelon. Imagine my surprise when instead of red, it was this beautiful golden colour instead! Apparently this is a naturally occurring version of watermelon, although this is my first time eating it. Tastes quite similar to the red variety, if perhaps a bit sweeter.

item.title: 23 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar →Next day

Today I exercised my democratic right to vote in the 2026 local and parliamentary elections of the Kingdom of Sweden at the Swedish trade representative office in Taipei. There I was given some home-made traditional cinnamon buns while chatting with a woman who had lived in Taipei for now 20 years.

item.title: 22 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar →Next day

A second (much better) attempt at cooking at home due to the continuing weather. At this rate of improvement I expect to cook the greatest meal mankind has ever made sometime next week. This is fried rice with pork, garlic, the rest of the Bok choi, and eggs, all sautéed in soy sauce.

item.title: 21 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar →Next day

Few things beat a hot bowl of noodles after being soaked by the Taiwanese rains. Hiding away from the shimmering lights of the city reflected by the drops of water, I am alone with my noodles for just a few moments.

item.title: 20 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar →Next day

Semi-failed first attempt at cooking in the apartment: Baozi (包子) steamed in an air fryer at too high a temperature served with Bok Choi fried in garlic and soy sauce. To drink, a glass of oolong tea (烏龍茶).

item.title: 19 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar →Next day

A small classic lunch consisting of a bowl of rice with pork braised in soy sauce. Most impressive of all is the price — only $40 (roughly 1 Euro)!

item.title: 18 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar →Next day

Another night market dinner, this time with my roommate, consisting of a bowl of noodles with a tea egg and some tasty fried balls of some kind. Not pictured is a cup of Papaya milk.

item.title: 17 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar →Next day

Some Taiwanese Fried Chicken (tfc) eaten at a night market close to home.

item.title: 16 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar →Next day

Some dànbǐng (literally egg pancake, a popular Taiwanese breakfast dish) filled with small pieces of pork tenderloin for breakfast. Woke up earlier today than usual, and found that there were still breakfast resturaunts open. Hopefully this means that I am slowly weaning myself off of the jetlag.

item.title: 15 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar →Next day

Wonderfully delicious Taiwanese beef noodles in a spicy broth.

item.title: 14 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar →Next day

Japanese Beef Donburi and a couple of Onigiri.

Today I woke up very late (due to being jet-lagged) and ended up talking to my roommate the rest of the day. By the time I realized I had not eaten for 24 hours all the restaurants were closed, and so I went down to the local 7-eleven and bought some simple pre-prepared meals. The Donburi was very good, but the fillings of the Onigiri were disappointing for different reasons.

item.title: 13 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar →Next day

This is the (appropriately named I might add) stinky tofu, one of the signature dishes of Taiwan. I ate it at a very popular and bustling restaurant with a wonderful atmosphere, but realized soon after ordering that I only had enough cash on me to cover the meal itself, not including anything to drink. “Not a problem” I thought. “I’ll go and have something to drink afterwards”. Lets just say I was practically running to the 7-eleven next door after paying.

item.title: 12 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar →Next day

Fried rice with beef; The first proper dinner in Taipei. Bought at a small restaurant in at the Shida night market near National Taiwan Normal University (ntnu).

item.title: 11 August 2026
item.description:
←Previous day Calendar →Next day

The second day of airplane travel, although what feels like one, continuous day. My flight was unfortunately grounded for 5 hours, meaning that my short 2.5 hour trip from Beijing to Taipei became almost as long as the original transcontinental flight from Stockholm to Beijing. The clear highlight was this candy that the kind woman next to me offered. I had thankfully brought some famous Swedish plockgodis that I gave to her in return.

item.title: 10 August 2026
item.description:
Calendar →Next day

What’s the deal with airline food?!

The first proper meal on this trip is chinese food — in the western sense — in a small heated package. Somewhat difficult to describe other than repeating the stewardess’ “Rice with beef” followed by “beef is spicy”.

Served with a clashing piece of smoked salmon in a bulgur salad with a piece of bread and small chocolate cake. Not pictured is a cup of hot jasmine tea and a copy of the Rénmín Rìbào (人民日报) that I was so graciously given as reading material while flying directly above St. Petersburg.
